steps.reason: Scope the dataset to the last 30 days before running any detection.
The query is broad ('is there suspicious activity?') with no specific entity or typology — a population-wide EDA summary is appropriate to understand the landscape before detection.
Compute per-account rolling features required by the rules engine, anomaly model, and risk scorer.
Run all named typology rules across the 30-day window to surface any rule-based flags.
The query is open-ended ('suspicious activity' with no specific typology), so an IsolationForest sweep is warranted to catch anomalies that rules alone might miss.
Broad suspicion queries should also check for network-level patterns (rings, fan-in flows) that neither rules nor anomaly models directly cover.
Combine all detection signals (rule hits, anomaly scores, graph findings) into weighted LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH risk levels per account.
